slides.title: Chunking / [legal] docs
slides.hook: Ask whether the liability cap covers lost Customer Data, and search hands back the cap, cut off at "do not apply to:".
inside: Where a size split drops the exceptions
Clause chunks with the section path on top
Long clauses: the lead-in on every piece
Cross-references, and when to move on

slides.title: The clause is / the [unit]
slides.text: A contract answers by clause, and a clause means what it says only with its number, its section and its lead-in.

steps: Find the structure: sections (8.), clauses (8.2), sub-clauses (8.3(b)).
One clause per chunk, with its sub-clauses.
Put the path on top: document > section > clause.
A clause over the size limit: split at sub-clauses and repeat the lead-in.
Store the cross-references ("Section 5.2") so you can fetch them.

slides.title: Search returns / the [cap]
slides.text: BM25 keyword search (`rank_bm25`) over each set of chunks. Query: "Does the liability cap apply to loss of Customer Data?"

options.output: Top hit: chunk 3, the cap in 8.2

options.note: Lifts the cap for missed backups

slides.after: The first top hit states the 12-month cap. The case that lifts it, 8.3(b), is in chunk 4, ranked second.

slides.title: Clause regex / still [merges]
slides.text: Clause numbers as regex separators, at `chunk_size=400`:

visuals.code:
seps = [r"\n(?=\d+\. )",      # 8.
        r"\n(?=\d+\.\d+ )",  # 8.2
        r"\n(?=\([a-z]\) )",  # (b)
        "\n", " ", ""]
RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
    chunk_size=400, chunk_overlap=0,
    separators=seps,
    {{is_separator_regex=True}})

visuals.label: Chunk 1 of 4 (heading lines shown)

bullets: Clause 8.3 now stays whole, but its chunk has no "Limitation of Liability" heading.
The splitter packs splits up to the size limit, so data protection and fees share chunk 1.

slides.title: Put the [path] / on top
slides.text: Each chunk starts with the document, the section and the clause number:

visuals.label: Clause chunk 6 of 11 (wrapped)

bullets: The chunk names its section, so search and the model both see the topic.
The answer can cite 8.2 by number. Store the number as metadata too.
Short clauses stay short: 114 to 222 characters here.

slides.title: Repeat the / [lead-in]
slides.text: With its path, clause 8.3 is 305 characters, over the 300 limit. Split it at (a), (b), (c) and put the 55-character lead-in on each piece:

visuals.label: Clause chunk 8 of 11 (wrapped)
visuals.code:
MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT >
8. Limitation of Liability > 8.3(b)
{{8.3 The limits in Sections 8.1 and 8.2}}
{{do not apply to:}}
(b) loss of Customer Data caused by
Supplier's failure to keep the backups
required by Section 5.2; or

slides.after: Each sub-clause now carries the rule it belongs to, the same way a table chunk carries its header row.

slides.text: 8.3(b) depends on "the backups required by Section 5.2". Pull the clause numbers out of each chunk at indexing time:
bullets: Fetch 5.2 with the hit: "daily backups of Customer Data for at least 30 days".
"Section 10" in 8.3(a) has no dot, so this pattern misses it. Match whole-section references too.
Chains of references need multi-hop retrieval, a later post.

cards.title: Use it when
items: Text has numbered clauses: contracts, policies, terms, regulations
Questions ask about one obligation or its exceptions
Answers must cite the section number

cards.title: Move on when
items: Your parser loses the numbering: fix the parsing first
Answers span chains of cross-references: multi-hop retrieval
Questions cover the whole document: summaries per section

slides.title: [Cheat] sheet
rows: One clause per chunk, with its sub-clauses
Path on top: document > section > clause
Clause over the limit: split at sub-clauses, repeat the lead-in
Leave short clauses short; keep sections apart
Store cross-references; fetch the cited clause with the hit
Join wrapped lines before matching clause numbers

slides.line: Transcripts break the same way: a size split can put a question in one chunk and its answer in the next. Split on speaker turns.
